Japanese billionaire Yusaku Maezawa announced in a January 1 tweet that he would give away 1 billion Japanese yen — about $9 million — to 1,000 random Twitter followers. His stated goal was to test the premise of a basic income.

Germany hosts nonprofit basic income initiatives, including Mein Grundeinkommen, which provides raffle-based cash payments to winners. Political debate continues, and the first city-level referendum on UBI will be held in Hamburg in 2025; no national program exists.

Basic income is supported by various politicians, economists, and think tanks, with proposals ranging from €400–750 per person per month; no national UBI program has been implemented.
Issued small grants to citizens of working age who had no other governmental support.

Spain conducted the “B-MINCOME” experiment from 2017 to 2019, providing a minimum guaranteed income to 1,000 households in Barcelona’s poorest districts; political and civil society advocacy for broader UBI continues, but no national program has been implemented.

Basic income is promoted by private initiatives, such as the Nimses project, which gives participants a daily allocation of 1,440 “nims” (time-based currency); no government UBI program exists.

Basic income is supported by academics and political parties, including Queensland Greens, Fusion Party, and Greens NSW. Proposals include a universal payment of $500/week for adults, with potential top-ups for pensioners, disabled, and carers. No national program has been imp…

In 2017, Utrecht and a few surrounding cities kicked off a basic income experiment with 250 recipients as part of a randomized controlled trial. Some recipients got the money (around $1,050 per month) unconditionally, while others had to do volunteer work.
Basic income has been promoted by the Vivant movement and philosopher Philippe Van Parijs, with a Belgian BIEN-affiliated network founded in 2012; no national UBI program has been implemented.

Universal basic income has been promoted by academics, activists, and several political parties including the Greens, Communists, Pirates, and Democratic Socialists, as well as supported by various NGOs; no national UBI program exists.
Basic income is supported by political parties LIVRE, PAN, and Volt Portugal; no national UBI program has been implemented.

Basic income is promoted by some economists and political figures, including proposals for a basic pension scheme and a universal basic dividend funded by capital returns; no national UBI program exists.

Basic income is promoted by the FNA Group and the Hungarian Pirate Party. A 2014 proposal suggested monthly payments to adults and children, but it received no significant political support and no national UBI program exists.

Switzerland held a nationwide referendum in 2016 on a proposed UBI of 2,500 CHF per adult and 625 CHF per child. The initiative, promoted by BIEN-Switzerland and Initiative Grundeinkommen, gathered enough signatures to trigger the vote but was rejected by 77% of voters; no nat…
The Bulgarian Union for Direct Democracy party, founded in 2014, included basic income in its platform, but no national UBI program has been implemented.

In 2022, GiveDirectly launched a universal basic income pilot in Liberia, in the country's southeastearn Maryland County. The program has reached 13,795 recipients, according to GiveDirectly. Villages in Liberia are randomly targeted, and all individuals receive monthly paymen…

Basic income is promoted by political parties including the Greens and Pirates, with historical support from the Red, Democrats, and Liberal Party. The NGO BIEN Norge advocates for UBI, but no national program exists.
Trial program gave 2,000 unemployed adults a monthly grant. Parliament declined to fund it past 2018.

Considered, but not yet implemented as of 2022. The Irish Government is running a Basic Income for the Arts pilot program. Any artist in Ireland could apply for the program, and 2,000 eligible people were randomly selected in 2022. The program provides a stipend of $350 a week…

Basic income has been debated by the Labour Party and other advocates as a potential replacement for existing welfare, emphasizing seamless income support and reduced bureaucracy. No national program has been implemented.
Pilot program in two villages paid roughly 8% of average income. Significantly reduced child malnutrition, increased school attendance, boosted community income, decreased theft.
Basic income has been considered in Lithuania’s policy discourse, with research and debate on its feasibility and potential to reduce poverty. However, no national UBI program has been implemented.
Basic income has been discussed by civil society groups and through European Citizens’ Initiative campaigns, but no national universal basic income program has been implemented.

Basic income has been discussed in Estonia by the Estonian Free Party and other civic groups, as well as via European Citizens’ Initiative campaigns. Parliamentary committees have reviewed proposals, but no concrete implementation has occurred.
Macau residents who hold a valid government-issued ID are given an annual payment to help compensate for the cost of inflation.
The Icelandic Pirate Party proposed a parliamentary resolution in 2014 to explore an unconditional basic income for all citizens; no national UBI program has been implemented.
